after.problem:
$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

Consider the surface integral of the function 
$f(x,y,z)=x+y+z$ 
over the parametric surface 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2},\,u-{v}^{2},\,{v}^{2}⟩
$$

for $(u,v)\in D⊆{R}^{2}.$ What is the missing expression?

*Hint: You can use the fact that $‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=2v\sqrt{1+8{u}^{2}}.$*
after.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=\sqrt{{u}^{2}+{v}^{2}+1}.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(x+y+z)\,{|}_{x={u}^{2}\,y=u-{v}^{2}\,z={v}^{2}} \\  & ={u}^{2}+(u-{v}^{2})+{v}^{2} \\  & ={u}^{2}+u\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,2({u}^{2}+u)v\sqrt{1+8{u}^{2}}\,\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the surface integral of a scalar function f over S is given by

∬Sf(x,y,z)dS=∬Df(r(u,v))‖ru′×rv′‖dA.

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product for our surface is

‖ru′×rv′‖=u2+v2+1.

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of r(u,v) into f(x,y,z):

f(r(u,v))=(x+y+z)|x=u2y=u−v2z=v2=u2+(u−v2)+v2=u2+u

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

∬Sf(x,y,z)dS=∬Df(r(u,v))‖ru′×rv′‖dA=∬D2(u2+u)v1+8u2dA.

content.problem:

$$

Consider the surface integral of the function 
$f(x,y,z)=x+y+z$ 
over the parametric surface 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2},\,u-{v}^{2},\,{v}^{2}⟩
$$

for $(u,v)\in D⊆{R}^{2}.$ What is the missing expression?

*Hint: You can use the fact that $‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=2v\sqrt{1+8{u}^{2}}.$*
content.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=\sqrt{{u}^{2}+{v}^{2}+1}.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(x+y+z)\,{|}_{x={u}^{2}\,y=u-{v}^{2}\,z={v}^{2}} \\  & ={u}^{2}+(u-{v}^{2})+{v}^{2} \\  & ={u}^{2}+u\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,2({u}^{2}+u)v\sqrt{1+8{u}^{2}}\,\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,-1⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨1,\,-1,\,-1⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+-{1}^{2}+-{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+1+1} \\  & =\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & ={x}^{2}-2yz\,{|}_{x=u+v\,y=u\,z=v} \\  & =(u+v)^{2}-2uv \\  & ={u}^{2}+{v}^{2}\end{aligned}

$$

after.problem:

{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A

Consider the surface integral of the function 
$f(x,y,z)=xy+z$ 
over the parametric surface 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,{u}^{2},\,2v⟩
$$

for $(u,v)\in D⊆{R}^{2}.$ What is the missing expression?

*Hint: You can use the fact that $‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=\sqrt{16{u}^{2}+4}$*
after.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=\sqrt{16{u}^{2}+4}.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(xy+z)\,{|}_{x=u\,y={u}^{2}\,z=2v} \\  & =u.{u}^{2}+2v \\  & ={u}^{3}+2v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,({u}^{3}+2v)\sqrt{16{u}^{2}+4}\,\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the surface integral of the function

over the parametric surface

$$

for $(u,v)\in D⊆{R}^{2}.$ What is the missing expression?

content.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=\sqrt{16{u}^{2}+4}.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(xy+z)\,{|}_{x=u\,y={u}^{2}\,z=2v} \\  & =u.{u}^{2}+2v \\  & ={u}^{3}+2v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,({u}^{3}+2v)\sqrt{16{u}^{2}+4}\,\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨2u,\,-3v,\,4v⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(-3v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(4v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,0,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(-3v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(4v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-3,\,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-8,\,-6⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨0,\,-8,\,-6⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-8)^{2}+(-6)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{0+64+36} \\  & =\sqrt{100} \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =x(y+z)\,{|}_{x=2u\,y=-3v\,z=4v} \\  & =2u(-3v+4v) \\  & =2uv\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if we denote 

$$
D={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 2,\,0\le v\le 2},
$$

our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}x(y+z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,2uv\cdot 10\,\text{d}A \\  & =5{∬}_{D}\,4uv\,\text{d}A \\  & =5{\int }_{0}^{2}2u\,\text{d}u\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2}2v\,\text{d}v \\  & =5\cdot [{u}^{2}]_{0}^{2}\cdot [{v}^{2}]_{0}^{2} \\  & =5\cdot 4\cdot 4 \\  & =80.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Evaluating Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces
content.problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}x(y+z)\,\text{d}S,
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by the equations

$$
x=2u,\,y=-3v,\,z=4v
$$

for $0\le u\le 2$ and $0\le v\le 2.$
content.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨2u,\,-3v,\,4v⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(-3v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(4v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,0,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(-3v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(4v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-3,\,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-8,\,-6⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨0,\,-8,\,-6⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-8)^{2}+(-6)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{0+64+36} \\  & =\sqrt{100} \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =x(y+z)\,{|}_{x=2u\,y=-3v\,z=4v} \\  & =2u(-3v+4v) \\  & =2uv\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if we denote 

$$
D={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 2,\,0\le v\le 2},
$$

our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}x(y+z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,2uv\cdot 10\,\text{d}A \\  & =5{∬}_{D}\,4uv\,\text{d}A \\  & =5{\int }_{0}^{2}2u\,\text{d}u\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2}2v\,\text{d}v \\  & =5\cdot [{u}^{2}]_{0}^{2}\cdot [{v}^{2}]_{0}^{2} \\  & =5\cdot 4\cdot 4 \\  & =80.\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(-u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(-u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,-1,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(-u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(-u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}-1 & -0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,0⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨1,\,-1,\,0⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(0)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =({x}^{2}{z}^{2}+y)\,{|}_{x=-u\,y=-u\,z=-v} \\  & =(-u)^{2}\cdot (-v)^{2}-u \\  & ={u}^{2}{v}^{2}-u\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,({u}^{2}{v}^{2}-u)\sqrt{2}\,\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$
